hypothesis: BrokerConn::write_request_deadline splits its BytesMut after each RPC, assumed to hand off capacity and trigger fresh per-RPC request allocations. Reusing the whole request buffer was expected to reduce allocations per RPC.
finding: The hypothesis does not hold with the locked bytes 1.12.1. BytesMut::split leaves the spare-capacity view in BrokerConn; after the completed payload is dropped, reserve reclaims the original backing allocation. A 10,000-request census records one 40-byte shared-allocation metadata promotion, with zero subsequent per-RPC allocations at all sizes through 16 KiB. A 64 KiB request additionally requires one growth allocation in both arms. Named producer data requests already use Worker.write_buf and BrokerConn::write_all_timeout rather than the targeted request encoder.
